name: Geryoneo
body:
Geryoneo
CR 10

This bronze-skinned giant has three bodies from the waist up, with three heads and six arms wielding weapons and shields, but only one pelvis and a single pair of thick, muscular legs.

XP 9,600
LE Large humanoid (giant)
Init +2; Senses all-round vision, low-light vision; Perception +22

DEFENSE

AC 24, touch 11, flat-footed 22 (+6 armor, +2 Dex, +6 natural, +1 shield, -1 size)
hp 127 (15d8+60)
Fort +13, Ref +9, Will +9
Defensive Abilities threefold body, threefold mind

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee +1 bronze shortsword +16/+11/+6 (1d8+7/19-20), +1 club +16 (1d8+7), +1 bronze-tipped shortspear +16 (1d8+7), 2 light bronze shields +15 (1d4+6)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks rock throwing (120 ft.), threefold presence

STATISTICS

Str 23, Dex 15, Con 18, Int 10, Wis 19, Cha 8
Base Atk +11; CMB +18; CMD 30 (38 vs. trip)
Feats Fortified Armor Training, Lightning Reflexes, Martial Weapon Proficiency (light shield, shortsword), Two-Weapon Fighting, Weapon Focus (club, shortspear, shortsword)
Skills Intimidate +17, Perception +22
Languages Common, Giant, Infernal

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Six-Armed (Ex)

A geryoneo usually comes into battle wielding three different one-handed weapons and three light bronze shields. It also will wear three bronze breastplates. Only one breastplate and shield at a time provides a bonus on the geryoneo’s armor class, but this bonus is not lost unless all three coordinated pieces are destroyed or disarmed. Since each head controls a torso and a pair of arms, all of the geryoneo’s three weapon attacks are considered primary attacks, but it attacks only once in a round with each one of its weapons, while using two shields to perform shield bashes as off-hand attacks.

Threefold Body (Ex)

A geryoneo’s vital organs and senses are spread across all three of its linked bodies. An effect that would cause it to become blinded or deafened instead affects only one of its bodies, unless it affects an area or targets each body as a separate creature. If one body is blinded or deafened, the geryoneo suffers no ill effects. If two bodies are blinded or deafened, it loses its all-around vision and is dazzled. A geryoneo is blinded or deafened only if all three bodies are blinded or deafened. It likewise has a 75% chance to ignore critical hits, sneak attack damage, and similar precision-based damage.

Threefold Mind (Ex)

A geryoneo’s heads think independently from each other, even if they are mentally connected and the giant has one will only. Every mind-affecting effect targeted at the geryoneo only affects one of its heads if the giant fails its saving throw. The torso and arms controlled by the affected head will stop fighting, but there will be no other effect unless all three the geryoneo’s heads fail their saving throw against the same mind-affecting spell or effect.

Threefold Presence (Su)

Once per day, a geryoneo can split its three bodies, fighting as three separate individuals at the same time. This functions as the threefold form spell, except for the following: the three bodies appear the same age; each body only has one head, two arms, and two legs; and the equipment worn by the giant is split between the bodies rather than duplicated.

Each body can make a full attack with its weapon, and one of the bodies dropping or giving away items doesn’t affect the other two in any way. The geryoneo loses its all-round vision, threefold body, and threefold mind abilities while this power is in effect.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate and warm islands and plains
Organization solitary, pair, or family (2-4)
Treasure double (+1 club, +1 bronze shortsword, +1 bronze-tipped shortspear, 3 bronze shields, 3 bronze breastplates, other treasure)

These hideous giants have three malformed upper bodies joined at the belly, each one well muscled and strong, with its own arms and head, all joined at the belly and supported by a single pair of thick legs below its massive trunk. The three heads of each geryoneo share a common mind, though each may have a somewhat different personality. A fully-growned geryoneo is about 13 feet tall and weighs over 5,000 pounds.

Geryoneos can interbreed with other giants, though their progeny are often malformed, with additional heads (though rarely the fully separated tripartite torsos of a true geryoneo).

These half-breed geryoneos have statistics identical to ettins, though they often have 3 heads rather than 2 and usually lack the vicious temperament and chaotic evil alignment of a typical ettin.

Geryoneos are pastoral creatures, loving nothing more than tending their flocks of sheep or oxen, husbanding them to prodigious size and fine fettle. They tend to keep to themselves but are taciturn and territorial, quick to anger against those that intrude on their solitude. They often train great hounds to defend their herds and flocks, and they have a particular affinity for orthrus chimeras (see page 45), sometimes infusing ordinary canines with their own tainted blood to cause them to sprout multiple heads like their masters.
